--- title: "Iteration" subtitle: Day 17 title-slide-attributes: data-background-image: ../img/horst_bakers_4.png data-background-size: 70% data-background-position: bottom right data-background-opacity: "0.8" data-slide-number: none format: revealjs: incremental: true code-copy: true code-link: true scrollable: true auto-stretch: false editor_options: chunk_output_type: console --- ## Recap from last class: Standardizing a vector Here's a short function that standardizes an input vector ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} standardize <- function(x, na.rm = TRUE) { (x - mean(x, na.rm = na.rm)) / sd(x, na.rm = na.rm) } ``` ::: Now we can easily standardize all of our variables, right? ## Cancer data ::: nonincremental - Set of digitized breast cancer image features - Row = an image of a tumor sample - Variables include the diagnosis (benign or malignant) and measurements ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Rows: 569 Columns: 12 $ ID 842302, 842517, 84300903, 84348301, 84358402, 843786… $ Class "M", "M", "M", "M", "M", "M", "M", "M", "M", "M", "M… $ Radius 17.990, 20.570, 19.690, 11.420, 20.290, 12.450, 18.2… $ Texture 10.38, 17.77, 21.25, 20.38, 14.34, 15.70, 19.98, 20.… $ Perimeter 122.80, 132.90, 130.00, 77.58, 135.10, 82.57, 119.60… $ Area 1001.0, 1326.0, 1203.0, 386.1, 1297.0, 477.1, 1040.0… $ Smoothness 0.11840, 0.08474, 0.10960, 0.14250, 0.10030, 0.12780… $ Compactness 0.27760, 0.07864, 0.15990, 0.28390, 0.13280, 0.17000… $ Concavity 0.30010, 0.08690, 0.19740, 0.24140, 0.19800, 0.15780… $ Concave_Points 0.14710, 0.07017, 0.12790, 0.10520, 0.10430, 0.08089… $ Symmetry 0.2419, 0.1812, 0.2069, 0.2597, 0.1809, 0.2087, 0.17… $ Fractal_Dimension 0.07871, 0.05667, 0.05999, 0.09744, 0.05883, 0.07613… ``` ::: ::: ## Standardizing cancer data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} scaled_cancer <- unscaled_cancer %>% mutate( Radius = standardize(Radius), Texture = standardize(Texture), Perimeter = standardize(Perimeter), Area = standardize(Area), Smoothness = standardize(Smoothness), Compactness = standardize(Compactness), Concavity = standardize(Concavity), Concave_points = standardize(Concave_Points), Symmetry = standardize(Symmetry), Fractal_dimension = standardize(Fractal_Dimension) ) ``` ::: ## > You should consider ~~writing a function~~ iterating
> whenever you’ve copied and pasted a
> block of code more than twice >—~~Hadley Wickham~~
>-Amanda Luby ## Iteration - Programmatically repeat the code - We have two options for doing this: + using a `for` loop, or similar (imperative programming) + `map`ping with functional programming ## for loops - `for` loops are the simplest and most common type of loop in R - Given a vector iterate through the elements and evaluate the code block for each . . . **Goal:** Standardize all of the numeric columns via for loops. ## for loops #### (1) Set up a object to store results ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} scaled_cancer <- unscaled_cancer %>% mutate( Radius = NA, Texture = NA, Perimeter = NA, Area = NA, Smoothness = NA, Compactness = NA, Concavity = NA, Concave_Points = NA, Symmetry = NA, Fractal_dimension = NA ) scaled_cancer ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 569 × 13 ID Class Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity 1 8.42e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 2 8.43e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 3 8.43e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 4 8.43e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 5 8.44e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 6 8.44e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 7 8.44e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 8 8.45e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 9 8.45e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 10 8.45e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA # ℹ 559 more rows # ℹ 4 more variables: Concave_Points , Symmetry , # Fractal_Dimension , Fractal_dimension ``` ::: ::: ## for loops #### (2) Determine an index over which to iterate Columns 3 to 12 are numeric, our index is `3:12` ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 569 × 13 ID Class Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity 1 8.42e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 2 8.43e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 3 8.43e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 4 8.43e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 5 8.44e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 6 8.44e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 7 8.44e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 8 8.45e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 9 8.45e5 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA 10 8.45e7 M NA NA NA NA NA NA NA # ℹ 559 more rows # ℹ 4 more variables: Concave_Points , Symmetry , # Fractal_Dimension , Fractal_dimension ``` ::: ::: ## for loops #### (3) Iterate through the index, standardize and save results
`i <- 3` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} for (i in 3:12){ scaled_cancer[, i] <- standardize(unscaled_cancer[[i]]) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 569 × 13 ID Class Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity 1 842302 M 1.10 NA NA NA NA NA NA 2 842517 M 1.83 NA NA NA NA NA NA 3 84300903 M 1.58 NA NA NA NA NA NA 4 84348301 M -0.768 NA NA NA NA NA NA 5 84358402 M 1.75 NA NA NA NA NA NA # ℹ 564 more rows # ℹ 4 more variables: Concave_Points , Symmetry , # Fractal_Dimension , Fractal_dimension ``` ::: ::: ## for loops #### (3) Iterate through the index, standardize and save results

`i <- 6` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} for (i in 3:12){ scaled_cancer[, i] <- standardize(unscaled_cancer[[i]]) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 569 × 13 ID Class Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity 1 8.42e5 M 1.10 -2.07 1.27 0.984 NA NA NA 2 8.43e5 M 1.83 -0.353 1.68 1.91 NA NA NA 3 8.43e7 M 1.58 0.456 1.57 1.56 NA NA NA 4 8.43e7 M -0.768 0.254 -0.592 -0.764 NA NA NA 5 8.44e7 M 1.75 -1.15 1.78 1.82 NA NA NA # ℹ 564 more rows # ℹ 4 more variables: Concave_Points , Symmetry , # Fractal_Dimension , Fractal_dimension ``` ::: ::: ## Putting it all together: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} # Preallocate storage scaled_cancer <- unscaled_cancer %>% mutate( Radius = NA, Texture = NA, Perimeter = NA, Area = NA, Smoothness = NA, Compactness = NA, Concavity = NA, Concave_Points = NA, Symmetry = NA, Fractal_dimension = NA ) # Iterate over numeric columns and save for (i in 3:12){ scaled_cancer[, i] <- standardize(unscaled_cancer[[i]]) } scaled_cancer ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 569 × 13 ID Class Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity 1 8.42e5 M 1.10 -2.07 1.27 0.984 1.57 3.28 2.65 2 8.43e5 M 1.83 -0.353 1.68 1.91 -0.826 -0.487 -0.0238 3 8.43e7 M 1.58 0.456 1.57 1.56 0.941 1.05 1.36 4 8.43e7 M -0.768 0.254 -0.592 -0.764 3.28 3.40 1.91 5 8.44e7 M 1.75 -1.15 1.78 1.82 0.280 0.539 1.37 6 8.44e5 M -0.476 -0.835 -0.387 -0.505 2.24 1.24 0.866 7 8.44e5 M 1.17 0.161 1.14 1.09 -0.123 0.0882 0.300 8 8.45e7 M -0.118 0.358 -0.0728 -0.219 1.60 1.14 0.0610 9 8.45e5 M -0.320 0.588 -0.184 -0.384 2.20 1.68 1.22 10 8.45e7 M -0.473 1.10 -0.329 -0.509 1.58 2.56 1.74 # ℹ 559 more rows # ℹ 4 more variables: Concave_Points , Symmetry , # Fractal_Dimension , Fractal_dimension ``` ::: ::: ## Your turn ::: {.task .nonincremental} Load the `palmerpenguins` package. ``` ::: ::: ## Preallocate storage to increase speed ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="2"} add_to_vector <- function(n) { output <- NULL for (i in 1:n) { output <- c(output, i) } output } add_to_vector(10000) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 0.12 sec elapsed ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="2"} add_to_vector2 <- function(n) { output <- vector("integer", n) for (i in 1:n) { output[i] <- i } output } add_to_vector2(10000) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 0.039 sec elapsed ``` ::: ::: ::: ::::: ## The difference is noticable for larger n ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="2,9"} add_to_vector <- function(n) { output <- NULL for (i in 1:n) { output <- c(output, i) } output } add_to_vector(100000) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ``` 6.38 sec elapsed ``` ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-line-numbers="2,9"} add_to_vector2 <- function(n) { output <- vector("integer", n) for (i in 1:n) { output[i] <- i } output } add_to_vector2(100000) ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ``` 0.438 sec elapsed ``` ::: ::::: ## Preallocating output Here are a few useful ways to preallocate storage for a vector of length `n`: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} output <- double(n) # numeric vector output <- integer(n) # integer vector output <- character(n) # character vector output <- rep(NA, n) # vector of NAs ``` ::: . . . You can make tibbles of NAs by combining vectors via `tibble()` ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} output_tbl <- tibble( a = double(n), b = integer(n), c = character(n), d = rep(NA, n) ) ``` ::: ## Create index vector Useful ways to create index vector to iterate over: - `1:n` - manual creation if you already have `n` stored - `seq_along(df)` - construct an index "along" the columns of your data frame/tibble e.g. `seq_along(unscaled_cancer)`
⚠️ Use this instead of `1:nrow(df)`or `1:length(x)` - `x` - pass in a vector, there's no reason it needs to be an "index" e.g. `colnames(unscaled_cancer)` ## Your turn: ::: {.task .nonincremental} Revisit the {palmerpenguins} `penguins` data. Write a `for` loop that calculates the `summary()` of a numeric variable and the `table()` of a factor variable. Store the results in a list (it will have length 8). ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: # `across()` {.maize} ## R has lots of alternatives to `for` loops - The basic data type in R is a vector - In R, an "integer" is the same as a vector of integers of length 1 - In more general-purpose programming languages, single items are stored differently than arrays of those items - This means that R is highly optimized for vectorized operations ## `across()` ::::: columns ::: {.column width="50%"} - `.cols`: columns to apply function to - `.fns` function to apply ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} across(.cols, .fns) ``` ::: ::: ::::: ## `across()` on unscaled cancer data ::: panel-tabset ### One Function ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} unscaled_cancer |> summarize(across(Radius:Fractal_Dimension, mean)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 10 Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity Concave_Points 1 14.1 19.3 92.0 655. 0.0964 0.104 0.0888 0.0489 # ℹ 2 more variables: Symmetry , Fractal_Dimension ``` ::: ::: ### Multiple Functions ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} unscaled_cancer |> summarize(across(Radius:Fractal_Dimension, list(mean = mean, sd = sd))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 20 Radius_mean Radius_sd Texture_mean Texture_sd Perimeter_mean Perimeter_sd 1 14.1 3.52 19.3 4.30 92.0 24.3 # ℹ 14 more variables: Area_mean , Area_sd , Smoothness_mean , # Smoothness_sd , Compactness_mean , Compactness_sd , # Concavity_mean , Concavity_sd , Concave_Points_mean , # Concave_Points_sd , Symmetry_mean , Symmetry_sd , # Fractal_Dimension_mean , Fractal_Dimension_sd ``` ::: ::: ### Mutate ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} unscaled_cancer |> mutate(across(Radius:Fractal_Dimension, standardize)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 569 × 12 ID Class Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity 1 8.42e5 M 1.10 -2.07 1.27 0.984 1.57 3.28 2.65 2 8.43e5 M 1.83 -0.353 1.68 1.91 -0.826 -0.487 -0.0238 3 8.43e7 M 1.58 0.456 1.57 1.56 0.941 1.05 1.36 4 8.43e7 M -0.768 0.254 -0.592 -0.764 3.28 3.40 1.91 5 8.44e7 M 1.75 -1.15 1.78 1.82 0.280 0.539 1.37 6 8.44e5 M -0.476 -0.835 -0.387 -0.505 2.24 1.24 0.866 7 8.44e5 M 1.17 0.161 1.14 1.09 -0.123 0.0882 0.300 8 8.45e7 M -0.118 0.358 -0.0728 -0.219 1.60 1.14 0.0610 9 8.45e5 M -0.320 0.588 -0.184 -0.384 2.20 1.68 1.22 10 8.45e7 M -0.473 1.10 -0.329 -0.509 1.58 2.56 1.74 # ℹ 559 more rows # ℹ 3 more variables: Concave_Points , Symmetry , # Fractal_Dimension ``` ::: ::: ::: ## Helper functions for `across()` ::: {.nonincremental} - `where(is.numeric)` selects all numeric columns. - `where(is.character)` selects all string columns. - `where(is.Date)` selects all date columns. - `where(is.logical)` selects all logical columns. ::: ## `across()` on unscaled cancer data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} unscaled_cancer %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), standardize)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 569 × 12 ID Class Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity 1 -0.236 M 1.10 -2.07 1.27 0.984 1.57 3.28 2.65 2 -0.236 M 1.83 -0.353 1.68 1.91 -0.826 -0.487 -0.0238 3 0.431 M 1.58 0.456 1.57 1.56 0.941 1.05 1.36 4 0.432 M -0.768 0.254 -0.592 -0.764 3.28 3.40 1.91 5 0.432 M 1.75 -1.15 1.78 1.82 0.280 0.539 1.37 6 -0.236 M -0.476 -0.835 -0.387 -0.505 2.24 1.24 0.866 7 -0.236 M 1.17 0.161 1.14 1.09 -0.123 0.0882 0.300 8 0.433 M -0.118 0.358 -0.0728 -0.219 1.60 1.14 0.0610 9 -0.236 M -0.320 0.588 -0.184 -0.384 2.20 1.68 1.22 10 0.433 M -0.473 1.10 -0.329 -0.509 1.58 2.56 1.74 # ℹ 559 more rows # ℹ 3 more variables: Concave_Points , Symmetry , # Fractal_Dimension ``` ::: ::: ## `across()` with a new function Let's say we want the range of each quantitative variable (`max(x) - min(x)`). We could name a new function, or we could do it directly in `across()` . . . ::: {.cell output-location='fragment'} ```{.r .cell-code} unscaled_cancer %>% summarize(across(where(is.numeric), function(x) max(x) - min(x))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 11 ID Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity 1 911311832 21.1 29.6 145. 2358. 0.111 0.326 0.427 # ℹ 3 more variables: Concave_Points , Symmetry , # Fractal_Dimension ``` ::: ::: . . . Or we can use an *anonymous function* ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} unscaled_cancer %>% summarize(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) max(x) - min(x))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 1 × 11 ID Radius Texture Perimeter Area Smoothness Compactness Concavity 1 911311832 21.1 29.6 145. 2358. 0.111 0.326 0.427 # ℹ 3 more variables: Concave_Points , Symmetry , # Fractal_Dimension ``` ::: ::: ## Your turn ::: {.task .nonincremental} Use `summarize` and `across` to find the *range* of any quantitative variables, and the *number of levels* of any factor variables in the `penguins` dataset. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} countdown(4) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
